hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated oxidising agent does to a C=C bond compared with cold, dilute conditions.
Remember that cold, dilute acidified KMnO4 gives a diol, while hot, concentrated KMnO4 cleaves the double bond completely.
Think about what happens to any aldehyde fragment under vigorous hot oxidation, and whether it can survive or is oxidised further.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two different KMnO4 reactions with alkenes**

Cold, dilute acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ gives mild oxidation to a diol. Hot, concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ gives vigorous oxidative cleavage.

$$\text{C=C} \xrightarrow[\text{dilute}]{\text{cold}} \text{diol} \quad \text{vs} \quad \text{C=C} \xrightarrow[\text{conc.}]{\text{hot}} \text{cleaved fragments}$$

**Choose the conditions to break C=C bonds**

The question says the C=C bonds are broken, so we need vigorous cleavage. That must be hot, concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4(aq)$.

**Work out the fragments from cleavage**

A useful rule for cleavage is to look at each C of the double bond:
$$\text{R-CH=} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} \quad \text{(carboxylic acid)}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{C=} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C=O} \quad \text{(ketone)}$$

**Allow for further oxidation**

Under hot, concentrated conditions any aldehyde initially formed ($\text{R-CHO}$) is immediately oxidised further to a carboxylic acid ($\text{R-COOH}$). Ketones resist further oxidation.

So aldehydes do not survive, and the final mixture includes ketones and carboxylic acids.

options.A: Incorrect. Cold, dilute KMnO4 gives diols, it does not cleave C=C bonds. Also aldehydes would not survive vigorous oxidation, they would become carboxylic acids.
options.B: Incorrect. The product pair ketones and carboxylic acids is right for vigorous cleavage, but cold, dilute conditions are wrong because they stop at the diol and do not break the C=C bond.
options.C: Incorrect. Hot, concentrated conditions are correct for cleavage, but aldehydes are wrong as final products. Under these vigorous conditions any $\text{-CHO}$ group is further oxidised to $\text{-COOH}$.
options.D: Correct. Hot, concentrated acidified KMnO4 cleaves all the C=C bonds in retinol. $\text{R}_2\text{C=}$ parts give ketones which resist further oxidation, while $\text{R-CH=}$ parts and any aldehyde intermediates give carboxylic acids as final products.
